subject: Post-demo: GDPR & SOC2 follow-up — DPA + SCC module recommendation
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.inference.com>
To: Claire Miller <claire.miller@neptunehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-04-15T15:12:00Z
Subject: Quick recap + next compliance steps (DPA / SCC / SOC 2)

Hi Claire — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so the team at Neptune Health can get what you need to move the evaluation forward:

- SOC 2 status: Redwood is currently finalizing our Type II audit — expected completion target is end of Q3 2027. We can share the SOC 2 readiness report and interim control descriptions now; full report once issued.
- HIPAA: Redwood supports HIPAA-covered workloads via a Private deployment and can sign a BAA for Dedicated/Private. For hosted API use cases we can discuss controls but BAA availability is typically on dedicated/private.
- GDPR / DPA: Attached is a first-pass DPA (Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.docx). Our standard position is that customers are the Data Controller and Redwood acts as Data Processor.
- SCC module: based on your description (Neptune is the Controller sending telemetry and patient identifiers), Module 2 (Controller-to-Processor) is the appropriate SCC flavor. If Neptune acts as Controller but you will pass data to downstream subprocessors, we should confirm Module 2 + Processor-to-Processor clauses as needed.
- Vendor security questionnaire: I see you have a short questionnaire — please send it over; Monica can own the intake and coordinate responses/evidence.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Claire — please drop the vendor questionnaire and any specific evidence checklist (ISO/SOC artifacts) into the Drive link above or reply to this thread.
2) Monica — take point on the questionnaire and pull the SOC-readiness docs + standard DPA.
3) Connor & Neptune legal — schedule a short call if you have redlines on the DPA.

Happy to sync any time next week.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0127

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.docx (DPA draft)

From: Claire Miller <claire.miller@neptunehealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Neptune Security <security@neptunehealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-16T09:24:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next compliance steps (DPA / SCC / SOC 2)

Hi Connor — thanks for the summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We've attached our vendor security survey (Neptune_Vendor_Security_Survey_2027-04.pdf) — it's ~12 pages, covers SOC/HIPAA/penetration test cadence and subprocessors.
- SOC 2: the security team will want to see recent control matrices and a description of how key controls are evidence-backed while final audit is pending.
- HIPAA: Neptune plans to process limited PHI in our proofs-of-concept; if Redwood can host that under Dedicated or Private with a signed BAA that's acceptable.
- DPA/SCC: our legal prefers a DPA that references the 2021 SCCs (Controller-to-Processor). If Redwood expects to use subprocessors for hosting (cloud infra, telemetry analytics), please list them or indicate where we can find the subprocessors list.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can you confirm current subprocessors and whether any are outside the EU?
2) Do you support data processing addenda that include Processor-to-Processor clauses (if we ever become a controller that passes data onward)?

I'll loop in our legal if we need a call. Thanks — Claire

--
Claire Miller
Head of Security & Third-Party Risk
Neptune Health
claire.miller@neptunehealth.com

Attachment: Neptune_Vendor_Security_Survey_2027-04.pdf

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.inference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-04-16T12:08:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Neptune vendor survey + clarifications (need DPA / subprocessors list)

Monica / Marissa — forwarding Neptune's survey and questions from Claire. Action items I see: 

- Monica: please ingest the Neptune_Vendor_Security_Survey PDF and populate our standard evidence packet (SOC-readiness memo, control descriptions, infra subprocessors list). They asked specifically where subprocessors are located and whether any are outside the EU.
- Marissa: curious on DPA approach — I attached our Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.docx in the original thread. Neptune prefers SCCs per 2021 Controller-to-Processor (Module 2 equivalent). Can Legal confirm whether our current DPA references the 2021 SCC framework and whether we should proactively include Processor-to-Processor clauses?

Timeline: Claire indicated they'd like the questionnaire back this week if possible. Can we aim to provide the filled survey + evidence packet by EOD Thursday (2027-04-18)?

Thanks — I'll be on the call if legal needs context.

Connor

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-04-16T13:36:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Neptune vendor survey + clarifications (need DPA / subprocessors list)

Thanks for the flag. Quick guidance from legal/product perspective before we fill the survey: 

- DPA & SCC: Redwood's standard DPA reflects the 2021 SCCs (Controller-to-Processor). Given Neptune's role as Controller, the Controller-to-Processor path is correct. We'll also include a Processor-to-Processor clause set (standalone annex) to cover cases where Neptune asks us to route data to another processor; that helps avoid rework later.
- Subprocessors: current subprocessors are (high level list): cloud infra (GCP in eu-west1), managed logging (LogStream Inc., eu-central), analytics (RedMetric Ltd., us-east with EU region option). I'll ask infra to confirm datacenter locations for each subprocessor and provide a CSV.
- SOC 2 in progress: we'll provide the SOC-readiness memo and the interim control mapping. For legal review, include the timeline to final report (end Q3 2027) and an attestation from our VP of Security.

Monica — please coordinate the survey fill and attach the following artifacts: control matrix summary (pdf), subprocessors.csv, SOC-readiness memo (pdf), and a short note on HIPAA/BAA posture. Aim for an initial pass by 2027-04-18 EOD. I'll review comments and handle any DPA redlines.

Marissa
VP, Legal & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
To: Claire Miller <claire.miller@neptunehealth.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:05:00Z
Subject: Completed: Neptune vendor survey + evidence packet (initial)

Hi Claire — thanks for the patience. Attached is our initial completion of your vendor security survey and the evidence packet requested. Items included:

- Neptune_Vendor_Security_Survey_2027-04_filled.pdf (survey responses)
- subprocessors.csv (high-level names + hosting regions)
- SOC_readiness_memo.pdf (control mapping + audit timeline)
- Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.docx (DPA draft — legal has annotated a few optional clauses)

Notes:
- Subprocessors: most infra is hosted in eu-west1 (GCP). One analytics subprocessors operates from us-east but we have a contractual EU-region-only hosting option; we've flagged that in the subprocessors.csv.
- SCCs: Marissa confirmed we will reference the 2021 Controller-to-Processor clauses and include an annex for Processor-to-Processor scenarios.
- HIPAA / BAA: we can sign a BAA for Dedicated / Private deployments; hosting PHI on our hosted multi-tenant environment is not covered by our standard hosted offering.

Next steps from our side: happy to hop on a 30-min technical/legal sync to walk through any redlines or evidence gaps. Claire, are you available 2027-04-19 or 2027-04-20 for a short call?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineering (Security Intake Lead)
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.inference.com

Attachments: Neptune_Vendor_Security_Survey_2027-04_filled.pdf; subprocessors.csv; SOC_readiness_memo.pdf; Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.docx
